column8: Tue 17 Nov: 3d context, one clause at most: Taiwan's fundraising law has receivers publish each gift as name, date, use and exact sum at least every six months; it binds the receiver, never Laura, and Taiwan legal questions are outside the case, so never legal advice.

Tue 17 Nov: store, beside row 1: the publishing rule also covers unsolicited gifts, so solicited is too narrow; whether Laura's contribution passes through such a body turns on the residency's legal form, which the case leaves out.

Tue 17 Nov: 3d, the team's sentence beside Laura's words: on a Taiwanese gift list the name is optional and the sum is not, the plainest local reason 3d leads with one figure ($115,000 on today's figures); no opt-out for the amount is read from the rules' silence, so S 4; context only, never legal advice.

Tue 17 Nov: travels with row 3 as its example (a NT$1m gift printed in full under a masked company name); two lists read via excerpts and the privacy statement itself not read, so quote only the printed line.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of row 3 (forms offer a name choice, never a sum choice); never as never whether the sum is shown, since a founder's gift is agreed one to one.
Tue 17 Nov: store, beside row 39: in a Taiwanese ledger a NT$720 gift and a NT$200,000 gift sit in one format; city bodies, not a residency.

Tue 17 Nov: store, possible 3e or Table 3 context on co-sponsors' own public raising (one year at most, a separate account, a use report); fills Q48's gap; Taiwan legal is outside the case, so no rule for Laura.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: a 15% cost ceiling on public raising is a cap, not the usual cost; the NT$85 line is Keel arithmetic at the cap and does no part's job.

Tue 17 Nov: store only: temple donor boards are custom, outside the fundraising law; why it runs deep is Keel's reading, and whether a temple building fund counts as religious activity was not tested.
Tue 17 Nov: accuracy guard only: any line naming Taiwan's fundraising regulator says the Ministry of Health and Welfare (since 2013), never the Interior.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q11d-016 (Foundations Act Art 25: donor lists with amounts each year); carry over the written advance opt-out and the fines; Taiwan legal outside the case.

Tue 17 Nov: store, 3d background: a Taiwanese foundation and the Ministry of Culture publish grants to the dollar, so a co-sponsor's share appears in its own list; one foundation, grants not building gifts.

Tue 17 Nov: aha reserve for 3d or the conceit's turn (the 1871 stone carved its own shortfall, 6.5% of cost, Keel arithmetic); fix the use: Laura's stated figure carries no gap line, but the facility's own accounts may, since her contribution does not rise with overruns (SKELETON 3d), so never Laura's plan has no such line for the building.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: a second stone with names, sums and a total; evidence for row 39, no part's job.

Tue 17 Nov: store, possible colour for 3d's trust point: the link through the character for trust is Keel's reading of three texts read via excerpts, so say it as ours, never as Taiwan's stated custom.

Tue 17 Nov: colour at most for 3e's dated NT$ line; fix: the stone gives no reason for dropping the sums, so why is Keel's reading; NT$3,500 is illustrative Keel arithmetic at the reform rate; never imply the NT$ could repeat 1949, since the dated NT$ line answers ordinary rate moves (NUMBERS 8d, 8j), not a collapse.
Tue 17 Nov: store, background to row 16 only: the 1949 swap of 40,000 old dollars for NT$1; history, never a forecast for the NT$.

Tue 17 Nov: store only: keep the ambulance stele (sums by name for a civic gift) once the thesis author and date are found; drop the lesson from the 1948 NT$ label, a heritage page's error that says nothing about Laura's NT$ line.

Tue 17 Nov: 3d judge's note with row 39 (Cloud Gate kept the temple wall and dropped the sums); fix the use: a NT$1,000 giver and the founder on the wall are not in the source read, so say names only, in the temple tradition, and leave gift sizes out; repeat givers named once is Keel arithmetic.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of row 39's two lists (a thank-you list counts people, a ledger counts money); its counts of unnamed givers stay as evidence there.

Tue 17 Nov: 3d or 3e client knowledge: temple foundations with steady income already give to Taiwan's arts (Longshan on Cloud Gate's 2026 list, Xingtian in Wenxin's gold tier), a co-sponsor kind to name; list order is unexplained, so never heads or leads.
Tue 17 Nov: store, 3d's recognition clause if room: the national venue thanks sponsors by stroke count with no sums, a neutral order the residency could use; one report.

Tue 17 Nov: store; fix the use: 3d leads with the top, $115,000 on today's figures, and says the bottom once as the part held since January 2028, so never the bottom as the fixed figure and the top as what more would buy; the report never prices what more money buys at the facility (no cost estimates).

Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q50-004 (Wenxin's four money bands and counts; NT$3.77m a bronze sum); adds that NT$3.11m (Keel arithmetic at 32.768) is bronze too; the award is repealed (row 25), so history only.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q50-003 (Wenxin dropped its money bands in 2025); carry the 8 Sep 2025 repeal and TAICCA's ESG award there; will likely report under ESG is a guess, never for 3d.

Tue 17 Nov: 3d's currency line and 3e: Taiwanese rules book a foreign gift in NT$ at the rate of the day or month it is given, so NT$3.77m at 32.768 (NUMBERS 8j) is labelled as today's size and the US dollar figure is what stays fixed; cite the 2026 college rule, since the award rule is repealed; pairs with Q11d-028.

Tue 17 Nov: store only: every university tier read holds NT$3.11m and NT$3.77m alike (Keel arithmetic at 32.768; only NT$3.77m is in NUMBERS, 8j); with 3d stating one figure, recognition of the range's width does no part's job.

Tue 17 Nov: 3d's recognition clause: say what is named for what share before anyone pays; fix: these are five universities' rules for their own buildings, never Taiwanese norms, and the report never estimates the facility's cost, so no claim on whose share passes half.
Tue 17 Nov: store, beside row 28: naming terms priced by share and years (a third for 20 years is Keel arithmetic); the over-half clause was cut off in the excerpt.

Tue 17 Nov: conceit turn beside 3d in the team's prose, never Laura's words; fix the parallel: the rule's line is the receiver's (money arrived), Laura's is the giver's (owned before stated), and in 2031 her money has not arrived either, so say Taiwan thanks by money in hand, Laura states by money owned; one college, may not must.

Tue 17 Nov: 3d checklist: a Taiwanese gift agreement names amount, use, naming intent, how it is shown and how it is paid; Q99-036 already holds amount, purpose and date, so this adds only how it is shown; a university, not a residency.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of row 39 (one body keeps a thank-you without sums and a ledger with them).
Tue 17 Nov: 3d, if named rooms are offered: a donor's name gives no ownership or exclusive use, which fits the residency owning the site (SKELETON 3d); a university rule.

Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q22-004 (building funders ask who pays to run the building) and Q75-044; adds a Taiwanese university rule; fix if used: the ten payments are a base for operations, never the whole running budget, and the operating reserve is the money set aside for them, not a second item.

Tue 17 Nov: store, 3d recognition colour: after 1999 a company that adopted a school could put up a marker only with the school's consent; Taiwan's largest wave of co-sponsored buildings is unsourced, so say a wave.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: the 921 relief foundation published each gift to the dollar; most of the 62 gifts were government transfers, so never as private building money.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: before 2006 no law made fundraisers publish; never say the 1999 earthquake caused the Act (no source read ties them).
Tue 17 Nov: store, 3d background: 921 co-sponsors published exact totals (the Red Cross NT$363,670,751 for 11 schools); disaster money, givers' own totals.

Tue 17 Nov: 3d judge's note, the card's synthesis: Taiwan keeps two lists, a ledger of exact sums and a wall of names, both of money that has arrived; Keel synthesis of 30-odd lists, so say none of the lists read prints a pledge, never that Taiwanese lists never do (pledges were looked for and not found, Gaps).

Tue 17 Nov: 3d, why it leads with the top: the contribution equals the stated top in every path (NUMBERS 4), so the figure co-sponsors count, $115,000 on today's figures, is the one a Taiwanese ledger would later print in NT$ at the day's rate; holds only if her money passes through a publishing body; re-check the figure after Wed 18 Nov's re-size.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: a gift to a state troupe expired into the treasury after its time limit; small sums, government bodies, no part's job.
